title: Relief demand forecasting benchmark task card
description: Supplementary S3. A machine-readable specification of the minimum information a public relief-demand forecasting benchmark task must declare before a reference baseline can be meaningfully distributed. It is a specification, not a dataset and not a fitted model: no benchmark result is implied.

quantity.description: What is forecast, e.g. people requiring emergency shelter, food rations required, displaced persons, emergency department attendances.

definition.description: Operational definition, including inclusion rules and how double counting is avoided.

ground_truth_source.description: Where the observed value comes from (distribution records, needs assessments, admissions data) and its known biases.

unit.description: Unit of the target, e.g. persons, households, kits, tonnes, attendances per day.

spatial_resolution.description: Administrative level or grid, e.g. admin-2, 1 km grid, facility.

lead_times.description: Lead times evaluated, e.g. ['72h before landfall', '0-72h after onset', '1-4 weeks'].

decision_served.description: The operational decision the forecast informs (pre-positioning, first distribution cycle, funding trigger, appeal sizing).

issue_time_rule.description: Which information is admissible at forecast issue time, to prevent look-ahead leakage.

hazard_scope.description: Uses the hazard categories of the review's master dataset so tasks can be linked to it.

rule.description: e.g. top decile of observed demand, or events above an operational trigger threshold.

severity_strata.description: Error must be reported per stratum, so that performance on surge events is visible rather than averaged away.

terms_of_use_verified.description: Must be true before a task is released; terms differ between repositories and some restrict redistribution.

split_rule.description: Train/validation/test split by event and time, never by random row, e.g. leave-one-event-out or rolling origin with events after a cut-off date held out.

baselines.description: The minimal baseline ladder every submitted model is compared with.

point.description: Scale-free metrics (e.g. MASE) are preferred because demand varies by orders of magnitude between events.

decision.description: Optional decision-relevant losses, e.g. unmet demand and over-supply costs, or trigger hit/false-alarm rates.

required.description: Whether predictive intervals or distributions are mandatory for submissions.

guideline.description: Reporting guideline the review recommends for prediction-model studies.

custodian.description: Who maintains the task and its versions.

link_to_review_dataset.description: Optional: study_id values in master_extraction.csv whose task this card formalizes.
